root_decision_sources.literal_tex:
## 01 — Opening cancelled clause and raised replacement

Viewed `readers/017/A/01_upper_correction.png` once.

The cancelled subject has a left upright and overlapping horizontal/diagonal passes; E_i remains the leading reading, but the cancellation does not settle the Sigma_i alternative. Select B's \unsure{E_i|\Sigma_i}, low, original C R01 subject retained, 0C. The following short verb remains \unsure{est|soit}, low: the connected/cancelled stems do not settle the alternative; the extra named alternative retains C's existing uncertainty, 0C. The adjective's short r opening, open rounded middle and final re favour rare; resolve that part of R01 to rare, medium (A/C), 1C. The X is followed by a distinct dark point inside the cancelled clause; preserve X. (H omission, high). Above the deletion the replacement on ait is visibly raised, agreeing with all three insertion states (H placement, high). The parenthesis begins with the connected s and dotted i of si, not H's où; select si, high. No mathematical expectation was used. The initial image call had failed without delivery; this exact existing PNG was then delivered once.

## 03 — Upper equality bars, row layout and endpoint marks

Viewed `readers/017/C/crop03_equalities.png` once.

Both left Sigma groups have long separate horizontal strokes above their complete plus/minus forms. Confirm the two overlines, high, recording S row SA01-K81-06 independently at both loci; C and H already carry them, 0C/0H. The equalities occupy successive rows; select the aligned source layout used by C and all three readers. The H qquad preserves the same reading order, so P01 is a noncount layout audit. After the first E_i, the visible points belong to the dotted i and there is clear blank space to its right; retain the first equality without H's comma, high, 1H. Far to the right of the second equality is a detached dark triangular point with a peaked top and broad base. Select reader C's complete M01 literal fill, qualified locally with period as the alternative, including its hspace placement. Its shape/presence is high confidence; the attachment and period function remain low confidence and the hand is undetermined. One physical point/role cluster, 1C/1H for this new qualification and literal reproduction, with component/placement metadata noncount. Do not add an ordinary period as a second mark.

## 07 — Complete slanted marginal note and neighbouring letter context

Viewed `crops/scan017_margin_context.png` once.

The rotated note shows introduire la partition: the opening word ends in a short rising r-like connector and final curved e, supporting introduire, medium, choosing A/B and C witness over reader C's added ending qualification and H introduisons. The partition letter has a high top and two legs with a curved right return; retain \unsure{\Pi|\pi}_j, medium, original C R04 first part retained. The heavy crossed form immediately before E_j has Sigma-like diagonal and bottom strokes, but its overlay remains crowded; retain \deleted{\unsure{\Sigma}}E_j, low, R04 second part retained. Retain the complete formula and closing brace from A's margin source. In this deliberately wider first crop, the short wedge reported by B after the brace is visibly the thick lower-left return of the S in neighbouring Soit: its loop/stem continues into that word on the main text line. Select A/C's attachment; represent it once through Soit, with a noncount component/coverage row, rather than a second free-standing margin glyph. Its attachment is medium confidence. H's terminal ill placeholder has no separately legible word following the note's closing brace in this crop. Preserve the reader disagreement about its possible referent; group the omitted crossed predecessor and the unspecified H placeholder under one marginal parent H difference, low, without claiming an exact positional identity for H's placeholder. Do not count the predecessor and placeholder twice. The adjacent Considerons and cancelled lower word are incidental context only; their accent/word decisions remain reserved for their planned crops.

Viewed `readers/017/A/06_cancelled_definie.png` once.

The cancelled word has a looped d, low e, tall f with descending return, followed by the short i/n/i/e sequence. Resolve original C R05 to \deleted{definie}, medium, selecting A/B. Its visible detached point belongs over a later i; the area over the e is blank. Preserve the unaccented spelling in both this cancelled word and the immediately following live definie, medium. Several strokes coincide with the E and the cancellation, so the earlier glyph remains qualified. Select reader C's \deleted{\unsure{\Sigma}}E_j, low, over A/B's firm predecessor. Original C R07 first part explicitly qualified this locus although its TeX printed a firm Sigma; retain that source doubt (0C), and record H's omitted old glyph once (1H). ## 12 — Short et and the live intersection word

Viewed `readers/017/A/08_intersection_start.png` once.

At the left a small e loop and tall t-like stem support et, but the heavy horizontal connection through it merges into the following word and does not settle whether that short word is cancelled. Select reader C's complete-state \unsure{\deleted{et}|et}, low. Original C R06 first part therefore has et letters resolved and cancellation state qualified; keep those components explicit under the same source row, one C physical-cluster difference for the new state qualification. The following connected sequence supports intersection, and its t/i/o/n ending is clear. The initial vertical/cursive entry is crowded by the preceding strokes; retain local case uncertainty as \unsure{intersection|Intersection}, low, combining B/C's lower-case primary with A's capital alternative. The word identity is supported but the original C R06 word doubt remains locally qualified, 0C for that component. Preserve this live word once on the baseline. H's struck intersection plus inserted intersection is replaced by the short et state cluster followed by the single live word; count one H parent difference across these connected state/word spans, with the second component noncount.
